PullRequest.Title: chat: load generated images in a square that only grows into the image
PullRequest.Body:

The image generation loader was a 320×50 strip, which read as clipped and as the wrong size next to the image it turns into. It now loads as a square sized to the shortest edge the finished image can have, so the reveal only ever grows it into the image. The loading and reveal animations are unchanged.

### Before / after

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the 320×50 strip expands into the generated image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eli-w-king/eli-vscode/image-gen-square-loader-media/image-gen-square-loader/before.gif) | ![After: the square grows into the generated image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eli-w-king/eli-vscode/image-gen-square-loader-media/image-gen-square-loader/after.gif) |

MP4: [before](https://github.com/eli-w-king/eli-vscode/blob/image-gen-square-loader-media/image-gen-square-loader/before.mp4) · [after](https://github.com/eli-w-king/eli-vscode/blob/image-gen-square-loader-media/image-gen-square-loader/after.mp4)

### Changes

- Image tools generate square, 3:2 and 2:3 images. The loading square's side is the shortest edge any of them is shown at: two thirds of the image size cap (`min(60vh, 400px)`), or, in narrow chats, two thirds of the width left beside the save action. It is rounded down to whole pixels, so no edge shrinks during the reveal.
- The reveal starts from the loader's measured size (`IChatImageRevealOrigin.size`), so the handoff from the loader to the image is seamless, for single images and in image batches.
- While a referenced image's bytes load, the pending square is also bounded by two thirds of the gallery's current width (the gallery is a size container) and of the image size cap, so it stays within the image if the chat or window resizes meanwhile.
- The batch preview's placeholder spans the preview, so its square is sized against the width the image will have.
- The `GlyphRevealFinal` fixture has a new `imageShape` input (Square, Landscape, Portrait) to see the square grow into each shape.

### How to test

1. Run the Component Explorer (`npm run serve-out-rspack`) and open `chat/generatedImages/chatGeneratedImages/GlyphRevealFinal`. The loader is a square. Select Complete Generation and it grows into the image. Switch `imageShape` and `narrow`: no edge of the frame shrinks.
2. With image generation available (`chat.copilot.imageGeneration.enabled`), ask Copilot to generate an image, in a wide and in a narrow chat. The loader is a square that grows into the generated image.

### Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/attachments/chatImageReveal.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatResourceGroupWidget.test.ts`: 58 passing (includes a delayed-reference test that narrows the chat before the image loads)
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts --grep "image|Image|glyph"`: 219 passing, 1 pending
- ESLint on the changed files and the pre-commit hygiene check: passed

The videos are recorded in the Component Explorer from the `GlyphRevealFinal` fixture, which renders the real chat widget and reveal, with the same sample image on both sides. Before is `main` at f7a95c34df1.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed geometry, GlyphSurface's unconditional visible rAF loop, and exact cell-loop scaling are directly established in repository code. The main uncertainty is device-dependent frame-time impact, not whether the PR adds the sustained work, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Main-thread canvas cell computation and drawImage/clearRect work on every animation frame
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with the loader's pixel area and display refresh rate for the full generation duration. In a typical wide viewport the grid grows from 32x5 (160) cells to 26x26 (676) cells, so per-frame cell evaluation/drawing rises about 4.2x; canvas pixels cleared rise from 16,000 to about 70,756 CSS pixels (and scale further with devicePixelRatio).
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Sustained CPU/rendering pressure while an image is generating, increasing battery use and risking dropped frames on lower-end, web, or remote clients
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The loader was a 320x50 band. GlyphSurface's requestAnimationFrame loop therefore cleared a 16,000-CSS-pixel canvas and evaluated/drew at most 160 10px cells per frame.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new 1:1 aspect ratio makes the same continuously animated GlyphSurface up to roughly 266x266 under the default 400px cap, without changing its every-frame full-surface repaint algorithm.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 22 adds `aspect-ratio: 1` while lines 20-21 size the loader up to two thirds of the 400px cap; this replaces the deleted fixed `height: 50px` and raises the animated canvas area and cell count by up to about 4.4x/4.2x.
Findings.Title: Throttle the enlarged loader's canvas repaint loop
Findings.Impact: Whenever generated-image progress is visible with motion enabled, GlyphSurface repaints the full square every requestAnimationFrame for as long as generation runs. On a wide chat this turns roughly 9,600 cell draws/second at 60Hz into roughly 40,560, which can cause visible chat/input jank and sustained CPU/battery use during slow generations.
Findings.Evidence: GlyphSurface.update schedules another animation frame whenever motion is enabled, and paintLoading clears the entire backing canvas then runs nested row/column loops that call drawLoadingCell/drawImage for every 10px cell. This diff changes only the CSS geometry from 320x50 to a square capped at 2/3 of 400px; tests confirm 200x200 under a 300px test cap, while the production default reaches 266x266. Batch ownership suppresses duplicate loaders within one batch, but the selected loader still performs this amplified work continuously on the UI thread.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the square visual but bound its animation work—for example, cap the loading-state repaint cadence (such as 30fps) and/or cache the static glyph field so each tick redraws only the moving wave—before increasing the surface area.

Scenarios.Scenario: A single generated image remains in progress, then reveals when embedded or referenced bytes become available
Scenarios.CriticalPath: While generation is running, the visible GlyphSurface schedules and paints on every animation frame; this is synchronous main-thread work on the interaction/rendering critical path. At completion, the new size getter performs one geometry read before the loader is removed, then embedded bytes can be assigned directly or referenced bytes must be read and decoded before reveal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read referenced generated-image bytes before assigning a blob URL to the inline image
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read for a referenced single-image result; zero for embedded/base64 data
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single referenced-image read was already required before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The reveal waits for this read and subsequent browser image load/decode

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser image decode followed by ImageSamples canvas draw/getImageData when reveal starts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One decode and one sampling pass per revealed image
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Decode and full displayed-image sampling already occurred before the geometry change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The reveal cannot start until decode; sampling executes synchronously at reveal start

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One effective loader per standalone generation sequence; cost scales with loader area, refresh rate, and generation duration. The new default wide-chat square has about 676 10px cells versus 160 previously.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Image-generation suppression ensures one active loader within a generation sequence. Glyph repainting is serial on the browser main thread. A referenced image has one asynchronous file read before browser decode/reveal; embedded data has no file read.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Glyph atlases are cached per surface and reused between frames, but the full cell grid and canvas are still cleared and redrawn every frame. Theme/resize invalidates the atlas. Embedded image data bypasses file I/O; referenced bytes have no new cache introduced by this diff. Image dimensions are retained per response for later renders.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: CSS dimensions, tests, requestAnimationFrame scheduling, and nested per-cell paint loops establish the changed UI-thread work directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact milliseconds and dropped-frame prevalence depend on device, DPR, refresh rate, and generation duration; the 2.5x-4.2x cell-loop amplification is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable materially amplified rendering regression: the square preserves one-loader ownership but multiplies continuous full-canvas repaint work without bounding cadence or dirty area.

Scenarios.Scenario: A batch of generated images shows one selected pending preview, then thumbnails and the selected full image as results arrive
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The selected pending preview owns one GlyphSurface and repaints every animation frame. When a selected result arrives, the new one-time getBoundingClientRect read captures its origin before replacing the loader. Referenced thumbnail reads and the selected inline-image read/decode must finish for those images to display, but are unchanged by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read each referenced ready image for its thumbnail
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one read per ready referenced slot, launched as slots become ready
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-ready-slot thumbnail reads existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each thumbnail waits for its own read; other batch progress continues

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the selected referenced image for the full inline preview
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read for the selected referenced preview, in addition to thumbnail reads
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The selected preview already performed this read before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Selected preview and reveal wait for this read

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Decode thumbnails/full preview and sample the selected image for the canvas reveal
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One browser decode per displayed thumbnail and selected preview; one sampling pass for the selected reveal
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Individual visuals wait for their decode; image generation and other thumbnails remain independent

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The animation remains one effective loader regardless of batch size because child tool animations are suppressed; its repaint cost scales with square area and duration. Existing image I/O scales with N ready referenced thumbnails plus one selected full preview.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One main-thread loader paint loop. Thumbnail readFile calls are launched independently for newly ready slots and may run concurrently; the selected full preview may add one concurrent read for the same selected resource. No limiter or concurrency change is introduced by this PR.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Thumbnail items and image dimensions persist for the batch view, avoiding repeated creation/measurement on ordinary updates. Glyph atlases cache only glyph sprites, not completed frames. Referenced thumbnail/full-preview byte reads are not coalesced here, but that behavior is pre-existing and unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: batch suppression, selected-loader ownership, asynchronous read call sites, and the changed geometry are explicit in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Real batch sizes and storage latency vary; the diff does not change I/O cardinality, while the selected loader's per-frame CPU increase is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: The only reportable regression is the same amplified one-loader canvas repaint cost; changed size capture and container sizing add only bounded one-time/layout work.

Scenarios.Scenario: The chat or window resizes while generated image bytes are still loading
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CSS container units resize the pending square; ResizeObserver schedules GlyphSurface.refresh on the next animation frame. That refresh remeasures style, clears its atlas, and repaints. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is added to the resize path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with resize notification frequency and the square's area; notifications are coalesced through a single MutableDisposable next-frame callback, while the ordinary animation loop already paints each frame.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Resize refreshes are coalesced to the latest scheduled animation-frame callback and run serially on the main thread alongside the animation loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resize invalidates the per-surface atlas, which is lazily rebuilt on the next paint. There is no cross-surface frame cache. No data cache or negative-cache behavior is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: container sizing and ResizeObserver scheduling are directly visible in the changed CSS and GlyphSurface implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Interactive resize frequency and platform layout cost vary, but notifications are frame-coalesced and no new external boundary is reached.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: resize work is coalesced and the changed code's dominant regression is already captured as increased full-surface per-frame painting.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and their relevant render, lifecycle, and image-loading call paths. Submitted one medium-confidence-in-impact, high-confidence-in-mechanism finding for the 2.5x-4.2x amplification of continuous main-thread canvas cell painting caused by converting the animated band into a square; no changed filesystem/network fan-out, cache lifecycle, or concurrency burst was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
